The page says the state held 'most of Shanxi and several parts of Inner Mongolia' in 907, minus Linfen, Hezhong, Jincheng and Qinyang (Qinyang, in Henan, is outside the Shanxi cells). Cliopatria's Later Jin 911 shape (71,612 km2) covers 46 percent of Shanxi; this shape is 1.8 times it by project cell count. The page does not locate the Hezhong command, so its disc is a reading; the Inner Mongolia parts are not drawn (the page names none).

ledger.note: 907: with the Tang gone, Li Keyong's Jin holds Shanxi from Taiyuan. 'At the time of the Tang dynasty's fall in 907' it held 'most of Shanxi and several parts of Inner Mongolia'; Li Keyong had been Prince of Jin since 896 and died in 908. The infobox gives no founding year; the extent is the page's wording turned into Shanxi minus the commands it names as lost.

912: Jin takes over Jincheng. 'In 912, Jin took over Jincheng.' The page names no month and no one from whom; Jincheng is one of the four commands it says Later Liang had taken (the later-liang-dynasty dossier carries no 912 loss). fx-29 (F145): the later-liang-dynasty dossier now carries the mirror loss (/ledger/2).

region.text: Liu Shouguang's Yan round You Prefecture (Youzhou)

ledger.note: 913: Li Cunxu's Jin conquers Liu Shouguang's Yan. 'In 913, conquered Yan' (Jin page); 'By summer 913, Zhou had put Yan's capital You Prefecture under siege' (Li Cunxu page). The Yan page's infobox gives 914 for the end; the Five Dynasties page gives 915.

ledger.note: 915: Tianxiong goes over to Jin. 'Zhang thus decided to surrender the circuit to Jin. Li Cunxu shortly thereafter arrived at Tianxiong and took over control of the circuit.' The page does not locate Tianxiong; the disc is the Wei Prefecture (Daming) country as in the later-liang-dynasty dossier.

ledger.note: 916: the north bank of the Yellow River goes to Jin. 'By fall 916, nearly all of the Later Liang territory north of the Yellow River had fallen to Jin.' The page names no towns; the region is the one the later-liang-dynasty dossier removes from Later Liang.

region.text: the lower Yellow River, the frontier between Later Liang and Jin

ledger.note: 917: Jin crosses the Yellow River. 'Jin forces attacked and captured the border fort of Yangliu', south of the river; fighting follows at Huliu Slope in 919 ('The battle ended in a draw').

922: Later Liang retakes Wei Prefecture. During the Jin campaign against Zhao, Dai Siyuan 'was able to attack Wei Prefecture and surprise the Jin garrison there, capturing it'. The page dates the attack to 921 or 922; 922 is used (as in the later-liang-dynasty dossier).

ledger.note: 922: Zhao falls to Jin. 'The Jin siege of Zhenzhou, therefore, was able to finally starve Zhang into capitulation in 922'; 'The territory of Zhao was then incorporated into Jin, which subsequently established itself as the Later Tang Empire.' Zhao lay 'in the area of Shijiazhuang Prefecture in central Hebei'; the page gives no month.

region.text: Zhaoyi circuit (headquartered in modern Changzhi, Shanxi)

ledger.note: 923: Zhaoyi submits to Later Liang. 'Li Jitao, fearing that Li Cunxu would eventually act against him anyway, submitted his circuit to Later Liang' in spring 923; the circuit was headquartered in modern Changzhi, Shanxi (later-liang-dynasty dossier).

ledger.note: 923: the Jin becomes the Later Tang (Tongguang era from 13 May 923) and the war goes on under that name until the fall of Kaifeng, which the later-liang-dynasty dossier dates to 19 November 923 and the later-tang dossier carries. This contest_end closes the Jin side only.

notes: Cliopatria row Former Jin (922-925, one shape, 135,053 km2, Wikipedia 'Jin (Later Tang precursor)', Wikidata Q6201794). It is the Jin of Li Keyong and Li Cunxu, a state in its own right from 907 to the proclamation of the Later Tang on 13 May 923, not a state of 922-925: the Yan page and the Zhao page both call it the successor ('Succeeded by Jin (Later Tang precursor)'), and the Li Cunxu infobox gives the Tongguang era from 13 May 923. Cliopatria files the same state's 911-921 years under 'Later Jin' (shape later-jin_911, Shanxi, 71,612 km2); the later-jin dossier marks that shape wrong and leaves it to this one, so this dossier adds new keyframes for 907-921 and does not review that shape id. The shared Wikidata id Q6201794 with 'jin' (the Spring and Autumn Jin, -750..-405) is a Cliopatria error: they are different states, the earlier on the Shanxi plain 1,600 years before; the id is kept here only because Cliopatria gives it. The Former Jin ends in 923; Cliopatria's 924-925 years are the Later Tang (Former Shu fell in late 925, Li Cunxu page) and belong to the later-tang dossier, which also takes the Later Liang realm on 19 November 923. Mirror events requested from this dossier by ea-04-c are present: the 915 Tianxiong gain, the 916 north bank, the 917 contest, the 922 Wei Prefecture loss, the 922 Zhao gain, the spring-923 Zhaoyi loss; the 912 Jincheng gain has no matching later-liang-dynasty loss. The Hezhong disc is a coordinate reading (no place in the gazetteer; the Hezhong command is the Yuncheng country of southwestern Shanxi, a reading); a gazetteer entry 'Hezhong' would replace it. Zhao (Wang Rong, capital Zhenzhou, 907/910-922) is a state with no dossier: suggested slug zhao-five-dynasties-period, group ea-04 additions. Yiwu (Wang Chuzhi, Dingzhou, allied with Jin) is another, not opened. Not drawn: Inner Mongolia parts held in 907 (the page names none); Jin's alliances with Zhao and Yiwu (allied, not vassal; the pages use 'ally' and 'allied'); Liao relations 922-923 (page silent, although Cliopatria lists Liao as a neighbour). Disagreements: Yan ended in 913 (Jin page), 914 (Yan infobox) or 915 (Five Dynasties page). Page budget 1-2 pages: five were opened (Jin, Zhu Youzhen, Li Cunxu, Zhao, Yan), because the mirror events of ea-04-c need dated pages.
